title: a tagged template, a new expression, an implicit super constructor, a for-of, a spread and a yield* all invoke a function whose capability row must reach the caller
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Inference': 'Calling a function with unsatisfied requirements MUST add those capabilities to the caller's R row' and 'Requirement inference MUST be transitive through ordinary calls.' Nothing in that obligation says the call has to be written as one. Every position here invokes a checked function the author never spelled a call for: a template tag, a constructor, a base constructor reached through a constructor the author did not write at all, an iterator method reached three different ways. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS: the row was dropped at EVERY invocation form that is not a call-expression node, on a backend whose inference walked call expressions and nothing else. The failure is silent and total — the function's row comes back empty, every downstream rule that consumes the row certifies the program, and the capability read aborts at run time. Six forms are in one case because they had one cause and would be fixed by one change; splitting them would produce six files that go red together and never apart. The IMPLICIT super constructor at line 40 is the sharpest of the six: `class Derived extends Base {}` has no constructor, no `super` call and no argument list anywhere in the source, so a walk over written syntax has literally nothing to visit, and the capability read is two declarations away from any token the author typed. The three iterator forms are deliberately three rather than one: `for-of`, a spread and a `yield*` reach `Symbol.iterator` through different lowering paths, and a fix that teaches one of them does not teach the others. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the coercion protocol members (`toString`, `toJSON`, `Symbol.toPrimitive`, `valueOf`) or a thenable's `then`, which are invocations with no call expression too but belong to the coercion family and have their own cases in this area — this case would otherwise go red for a coercion defect and be read as an invocation-form one. It also does not pin a DECORATOR, which is measured identical on both backends but only with the modern `(value, context)` signature; the legacy two-argument spelling type-checks under the CLI's options and not under a bare option set, and a case whose green depends on which option set ran is a case that will break for the wrong reason. It also does not pin the diagnostics' ORDER, which the judge compares as a sorted multiset. `messageContains` is declared once and holds all six to Db, because six refusals at six positions are satisfied by code and position alone whatever the row named; it is the bare capability name because the backends render a row as `Db` and `{Db}`. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the third declared line from 40 to 39 — collapsing the implicit-super row onto the explicit-constructor row, which is what a backend that resolved `new Derived()` to `Constructed` would produce — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 d39a7afa6a72426dd0cb569b653efaeca8bfb15e4f065caa3b5c4502528f69ec before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The paired negative control is `ordinary-invocation-forms-with-no-call-expression-charge-nothing`, the same six forms over callees that read nothing, which must keep compiling AND RUNNING.
